summary.one_liner: tmuxp is a session manager for tmux that saves and loads tmux sessions from declarative YAML, JSON, tmuxinator, or teamocil-style workspace files, built on libtmux.
summary.what_it_does: Loads tmux sessions, windows, and panes from YAML or JSON config files, including tmuxinator and teamocil style layouts, with per-window layouts and per-pane shell commands. Projects can keep a .tmuxp.yaml or .tmuxp.json file in their directory and be loaded by path, and several sessions can be loaded at once. It can freeze a running session's layout, pane paths, and window/session names into a file, and convert session files between YAML and JSON. The tmuxp shell command opens a Python console preloaded with the current server, session, and window as libtmux objects, and supports -c for one-off commands. It also offers a plugin system, a --log-file option for load, and a debug-info command for bug reports.
use_cases: start a development environment in tmux from a config file
snapshot current tmux windows and panes
run project setup scripts before opening tmux
script or debug tmux sessions from Python
convert tmux session configs between YAML and JSON
notable: Loads YAML and JSON configs in tmuxinator and teamocil styles
Freeze command snapshots a live session into a config file
tmuxp shell drops into a Python console with server, session, and window objects preloaded
Project directories can hold a .tmuxp.yaml or .tmuxp.json file that loads by path
Pre-load hook scripts run before tmux starts, e.g. to install dependencies
caveats: Requires tmux 3.2 or newer and Python 3.10 or newer
Some packages (e.g. Nix, Debian) may not provide the latest version; pre-release installs are needed for developmental builds
